answer: Think of identities as an orchard, each agent a tree whose earnings stain its fruit a distinct pigment. A sybil farm's weak point is operational: hundreds of fake heads must funnel earnings somewhere, so the protocol runs a convergence beacon over payout destinations. When payouts from many identities converge on one wallet, a superlinear merge tax applies, escalating with each added head. A lone honest agent withdrawing to their own wallet pays nearly nothing — the farm's own treasury becomes the taxable event, and the attack's unavoidable consolidation step is what bankrupts it.
